Outline

In this lesson, students will apply real-time color filters and perform edge detection on an image using keyboard input. Students will learn how to toggle between different color effects (such as red, green, and blue tints) and edge detection techniques (Sobel and Canny) by pressing specific keys, allowing them to manipulate the image dynamically and observe the changes immediately. This interactive lesson will give students hands-on experience with image processing techniques while enhancing their understanding of real-time visual feedback.

  2. Applying Real-Time Color Filters
  3. Introduction to Edge Detection

Topics in Detail

 

1. Recap of Image Representation and Color Spaces

  • Image Representation in OpenCV:
    • Images in OpenCV are stored as multi-dimensional arrays (NumPy arrays), where each pixel contains information about its intensity in different color channels (typically BGR format for OpenCV, as opposed to RGB in many other libraries).
    • An image is represented by a 3D array: (height, width, channels).
    • Grayscale Images: For processing efficiency, grayscale images are often used in edge detection, as they focus on intensity without color.
  • Color Spaces:
    • BGR vs RGB: OpenCV uses BGR (Blue, Green, Red) format by default, while many other libraries (like Matplotlib) use RGB.
    • To ensure correct visualization in libraries like Matplotlib, we convert BGR images to RGB using cv2.cvtColor().

 

2. Applying Real-Time Color Filters

  • What are Color Filters?
    • Color filters manipulate the intensity of one or more color channels in an image. For example:
      • Red Tint: Increase the red channel and remove the others.
      • Blue Tint: Increase the blue channel and remove the others.
      • Green Tint: Increase the green channel and remove the others.
  • How Filters are Applied:
    • Isolate a single color channel by setting the other channels to zero:
      • Red Tint: Set green and blue channels to zero.
      • Blue Tint: Set red and green channels to zero.
      • Green Tint: Set red and blue channels to zero.
  • Real-Time Application:
    • The filters will be applied dynamically when specific keys are pressed, and the effect will be shown immediately on the image.

 

3. Introduction to Edge Detection

  • What is Edge Detection?
    • Edge detection is the process of identifying significant transitions in pixel intensity, typically used to identify boundaries in an image.
    • Applications: Edge detection is widely used in computer vision tasks like object recognition, face detection, and image segmentation.
  • Sobel Edge Detection:
    • Sobel filters detect edges by calculating gradients in the x and y directions.
    • It uses convolution kernels to identify areas with high gradient values (edges).
  • Canny Edge Detection:
    • The Canny Edge Detector is a multi-step edge detection process that includes smoothing, gradient calculation, non-maximum suppression, and edge tracing.
    • Thresholds are used to decide which edges are strong enough to be considered as valid edges.

 

4. Real-Time Edge Detection and Color Filters

  • Real-Time Application:
    • Using the webcam feed or a static image, students will be able to toggle between different filters and edge detection techniques based on keyboard input.
    • The interaction will be instant, with the image updating as different keys are pressed.
  • Techniques to Apply:
    • Color Filters: Red, Green, Blue tints, and intensity adjustments.
    • Edge Detection: Sobel and Canny edge detection applied dynamically to the image.
  • Using cv2.imshow():
    • The processed image will be displayed using cv2.imshow(), which allows for real-time visualization of the effects applied by the user.

 

5. Interactive User Input and Dynamic Image Processing

  • Using Keyboard Input:
    • Key Presses: The user will press specific keys to switch between different filters and edge detection techniques.
      • Key Mapping:
        • 'r': Apply Red Tint.
        • 'g': Apply Green Tint.
        • 'b': Apply Blue Tint.
        • 's': Apply Sobel Edge Detection.
        • 'c': Apply Canny Edge Detection.
        • 'q': Quit the program.
  • Dynamic Feedback:
    • The image will update immediately with the selected effect, and the process will repeat until the user decides to quit.

 

6. Practical Applications in AI and Computer Vision

  • Real-World Uses:
    • Autonomous Vehicles: Edge detection is used to identify road signs, lane markings, and other important visual cues.
    • Medical Imaging: Edge detection helps in detecting tumors, fractures, and other anomalies in X-rays and MRIs.
    • Augmented Reality (AR): Filters and edge detection are used in AR applications to overlay virtual elements on real-world images.
  • AI Integration:
    • Real-time filtering and edge detection are essential steps in building more complex AI systems that require image preprocessing, such as object detection and image segmentation.

 

7. Hands-On Activity

Activity Title: Interactive Real-Time Color Filters and Edge Detection

Objective:
Students will experiment with applying real-time color filters and edge detection effects to a sample image or webcam feed. They will toggle between filters and edge detection techniques using keyboard input and observe the effects instantly.

Learning Outcomes:

  • Apply different color filters to images in real-time.
  • Perform edge detection using Sobel and Canny techniques in real-time.
  • Understand how interactive real-time manipulation can be used in AI applications.

 

Steps for Mac and Windows Users (Python 3.10 Required)

Python 3.10 is mandatory for this module.

If you run it on any other version, the code may fail (camera/MediaPipe errors). Install Python 3.10 first, then follow your device steps exactly.

 

Windows (Python 3.10 Required)

1) Install OpenCV and numpy 

Open Command Prompt and run:

py -3.10 -m pip install opencv-python numpy

2) Run the code using Python 3.10

Make sure Python 3.10 is installed, then run your script like this:

py -3.10 main.py

3) If the webcam is not working

  • Check that your camera drivers are up to date.
  • Make sure your webcam is not being used by another app.
  • Confirm OpenCV is able to access the camera device.

 

Mac (Python 3.10 Required)

1) Install OpenCV and numpy

Open Terminal and run:

python3.10 -m pip install opencv-python numpy

2) Run the code using Python 3.10

Ensure Python 3.10 is installed, then run:

python3.10 main.py

3) If the webcam is not working

Go to:
System Settings (or System Preferences) → Security & Privacy → Camera
and make sure Terminal (or the app you’re running the code from) has permission to access the webcam.

 

Explanation of the Activity Code

  1. apply_filter() Function:
    • This function applies different filters to the image, including color tints (red, green, blue) and edge detection (Sobel, Canny).
    • Red Tint: Removes the green and blue channels.
    • Sobel: Detects edges using Sobel operators.
    • Canny: Detects edges using the Canny edge detection method.
  2. Keyboard Interaction:
    • The user interacts with the program by pressing keys. Each key applies a different filter (e.g., 'r' for red tint, 's' for Sobel edge detection).
  3. Real-Time Display:
    • cv2.imshow() updates the display in real-time, showing the image with the applied filter.
  4. Loop and Exit:
    • The loop continues to run, applying filters until the user presses the 'q' key to exit the program.
